title: Introduce RAG Interactive Scenario Editor with Live Tool Mocks and Contract-Aware Snippets
author: Aditi Menon
release_notes: Adds a developer-facing interactive scenario editor playground for composing RAG/agent scenarios with live tool mocks and contract linting. No runtime or infra changes.
description:
Motivation: Engineers and solutions teams repeatedly asked for a compact, browser-first playground where they can author, iterate, and replay RAG/agent scenarios with deterministic tool-call mocks and immediate contract-aware feedback. Existing quickstarts show how to wire tool-calling and retrieval but are fragmented across examples and lack a unified, low-friction authoring loop.

This PR introduces an interactive Scenario Editor playground (static frontend + lightweight dev proxy) under redwood-examples/interactive-scenario-editor. The editor lets users: author a stepwise scenario (series of user messages, retrieval steps, tool calls); attach typed tool contract stubs (JSON schema) and see a live lint report; run a deterministic replay using built-in mock responses; and export the scenario as a RAG Quickstart bundle (manifest + sample prompts) for CI/evals. The playground is self-contained (no external cloud credentials required) and designed for rapid iteration during local development.

Main features: in-browser scenario composer with drag-drop steps and YAML/JSON editor view; contract linter panel that validates tool call payloads against declared JSON schemas and highlights mismatches inline; live tool mock registry to define mock responses per tool and per step; replay runner with tokenized trace and structured output diff view; exporter that generates a validated quickstart scaffold (TS/py examples and telemetry probe hooks).

Scope: exporter emits a validated quickstart bundle that callers can adopt into CI or local quickstarts. No changes to Redwood API surface or backend telemetry ingestion. The dev proxy is intended for local testing and CI only.
commits: feat(editor): initial interactive composer and UI scaffolding
feat(linter): ajv-based contract validation and rule set
feat(replay): deterministic runner, trace format and exporter
feat(mocks): simple mock registry and editor
test: add unit tests for linter and replay harness
ci: add headless replay smoke job to GitHub Actions
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Nice UX — can we make the exported bundle include a minimal telemetry probe? (author: added follow-up FG ticket; export kept minimal in this PR)
Sofia Ramirez: Linter flags are helpful but the error overlay is noisy at small viewports. Suggest collapsing by default on mobile. (author: adjusted panel default state and added collapse toggle)
Diego Alvarez: CI flaky on first run because headless browser timed out. (author: increased timeout and added retry; second run passed)
ci_checks: GitHub Actions: headless-replay-smoke - pass (2 retries for puppeteer)
testing: Unit: replay harness deterministic traces (seeded RNG)
E2E smoke: headless run of a seed scenario in CI using puppeteer
Manual: local dev playthrough and export bundle validation
examples_snippets:
# Example exported scenario manifest (YAML)
name: onboarding-example
version: 0.1.0
steps:
  - type: user_message
    content: "How do I reset my password?"
  - type: retrieve
    index: support-articles
  - type: tool_call
    tool: http_helpdesk
    input_schema: http_tool_schema.json

// Quickstart exporter CLI example
pnpm --filter ./redwood-examples/interactive-scenario-editor run export --scenario onboarding.scenario.yaml --out ../quickstarts/onboarding-example
observability_notes: No production telemetry changes in this PR. Added optional telemetry hooks in exporter to surface a minimal smoke probe (disabled by default).
README documents how to add Redwood Console telemetry probe snippets once an exported quickstart is adopted.
